notes: No candidate won a majority of the electoral votes, so the House of Representatives chose the president in a contingent election on February 9, 1825, voting by state delegation. John Quincy Adams won 13 delegations to Andrew Jackson’s 7 and William H. Crawford’s 4, and became president although Jackson had led in both the popular and the electoral vote.
John C. Calhoun was elected vice president with 182 electoral votes.
All four candidates who won electoral votes were Democratic-Republicans.
In Delaware, Georgia, Louisiana, New York, South Carolina and Vermont the legislature chose the electors, so those states had no popular vote.
Illinois, Kentucky, Maryland, Missouri and Tennessee chose their electors by district. Maine chose two electors statewide and the rest by district.
Delaware, Illinois, Louisiana, Maryland and New York split their electoral votes.
With the corrected returns in several states, Adams has 113,464 votes added up state by state, close to the American Presidency Project’s 113,122. Wikipedia’s national table gives him 122,440.
